`parseDigits` returns `NaN` when the string has no parseable digits. `parseInt(str, 10)` yields `NaN`, so it falls into the fallback branch, accumulates an empty string `""` (no Han decimal or non-Latin digit characters matched), and returns `parseInt("", 10)`, which is `NaN`. (Note it returns a number in that case, not `""` — the empty string is only an intermediate accumulator.)

It returns the two-element array `[null, {}]`: `input.match(regex)` yields `null` when there is no match, and the function then returns `[matches, {}]`, i.e. `null` as the raw match result plus an empty object as the parsed token map. (On a successful match it returns `[matches, all]`, where `all` maps token names to deserialized values.)

It returns an `Invalid` object (truthy), not `false`. `isInteger(obj.weekYear)` is false, so it returns `unitOutOfRange("weekYear", obj.weekYear)`, i.e. `new Invalid("unit out of range", "you specified <weekYear> (of type <typeof weekYear>) as a weekYear, which is invalid")`. It only returns `false` when weekYear is an integer and both weekNumber and weekday are valid.

It returns `LocalZone.instance` — the getter is `return defaultZone || LocalZone.instance;`, so a null internal `defaultZone` falls back to the local zone singleton (the module deliberately doesn't initialize `defaultZone` to `LocalZone.instance` directly because of loading-order issues).

Fixed and verified. Root cause: `Interval.fromISO` called `DateTime.fromISO` (and `Duration.fromISO`) on both halves before deciding which half was a date and which was a duration, so with `Settings.throwOnInvalid = true` a valid `<start>/<duration>` (or `<duration>/<end>`) string threw before the duration fallback could run. It now probes each half in a try/catch and only falls back to `Interval.invalid("unparsable", ...)` when nothing parses. Verified: `npx jest test/interval` 127/127 pass, full suite unchanged apart from 2 pre-existing French-ICU `toFormat` failures, plus ad-hoc checks that valid date/duration forms no longer throw and invalid input still throws under `throwOnInvalid`.

Fixed and verified. Root cause: in `objToLocalTS` (src/impl/util.js), the year 0–99 correction did `d.setUTCFullYear(d.getUTCFullYear() - 1900)`. `Date.UTC` had already normalized any month/day overflow against year 2000 (a leap year), and then only the year was rewritten to 100 (not a leap year), so a `plus`/`minus` crossing year 100 through February landed one day early (e.g. `0099-12-31` + 61 days gave `0100-03-01` instead of `0100-03-02`). It now re-sets year, month and day together (`d.setUTCFullYear(obj.year, obj.month - 1, obj.day)`) so the overflow is re-normalized against the real target year. Verified: exhaustive check of all year-99 start dates × 0–120 added days shows 0 mismatches (1596 before), `npx jest test/datetime` and the full suite show no new failures (only the 2 pre-existing French-ICU `toFormat` failures).

It resets the default zone to the local zone: the setter is `if (!z) { defaultZone = null; } else { defaultZone = normalizeZone(z); }`, so a falsy value (e.g. `""`) sets the internal `defaultZone` to `null`, and the `defaultZone` getter then falls back to `LocalZone.instance`. (Note that `Settings.defaultZoneName` would then report `"local"`.)
On it — investigating the src/impl/util.js padding bug behind `DateTime#toISODate() correctly pads negative years`. ETA ~12 min. (Bugs #8 and #11 are still in progress.)

It's an abstract getter: it just `throw new ZoneIsAbstractError()`. `Zone` is an interface — concrete subclasses (LocalZone, IANAZone, FixedOffsetZone, InvalidZone) override `type` to return their zone type string ("local", "iana", "fixed", "invalid").

A `FixedOffsetZone` built from the parsed offset: `if (!isUndefined(matches.Z)) { zone = new FixedOffsetZone(matches.Z); }`. So the zone returned (as the second element of the `[vals, zone]` pair) is a fixed-offset zone for that offset; if `Z` is undefined it falls back to `IANAZone.create(matches.z)` for a named zone, else `null`.

Fixed and verified. Root cause: in src/duration.js the conversion matrices lacked two entries, so some unit pairs converted to NaN (masked to 0 by the `values[u] || 0` getters): `years.quarters` was missing in both the casual and accurate matrices, and `quarters.seconds` was missing in the casual matrix. Added `quarters: 4` to both `years` entries and `seconds: 91 * 24 * 60 * 60` to casual `quarters`. Verified with a systematic all-pairs checker (every ordered pair of the 9 units × both conversionAccuracy values × positive/negative magnitudes): 3 checks failed before, all pass after; `npx jest test/duration` 114/114 pass and the full suite shows no new failures (only the 2 pre-existing French-ICU toFormat failures).
On it — investigating the src/zones/fixedOffsetZone.js bug (invalid fixed-offset zones should make the zone and any DateTime in it invalid). ETA ~12 min. (Bugs #8 and #15 are still in progress.)

`hour === 24` is valid only when the rest of the time is zero: the check is `integerBetween(hour, 0, 23) || (hour === 24 && minute === 0 && second === 0 && millisecond === 0)`. So 24:00:00.000 is accepted (end-of-day), but 24:00:00.001 or 24:30 is not.

Fixed and verified. Root cause: `padStart` in src/impl/util.js padded the signed string form of the number, so the minus sign was counted as a digit and zeros could land after the sign (or the sign could be sliced off): `padStart(-1, 4)` gave `"00-1"`, making `DateTime.utc(-1,1,1).toISODate()` return `"00-1-01-01"`, and `-100` was left unpadded. It now pads the absolute value and re-attaches the sign: `padStart(-1,4) === "-0001"`, `padStart(-100,4) === "-0100"`, `padStart(12,4) === "0012"`, with non-negative and already-wide inputs unchanged. Verified: `DateTime.utc(-100,1,1).toISODate() === "-0100-01-01"`, `DateTime.utc(-1,1,1).toISO() === "-0001-01-01T00:00:00.000Z"`, positive dates and `formatOffset`/`Formatter.num` callers unchanged, and the full suite shows no new failures (only the 2 pre-existing French-ICU toFormat failures).
